deviations.what: Missing cpc_subclass values are recoded to the literal string "NA" and then kept, so missing becomes a real class that is counted in n_base_classes, n_forward_classes and new_classes (and a firm whose only base patents lack a class gets a non-NA new_classes instead of NA under rule 8), whereas the spec says a missing class contributes nothing.

notes: Everything else matches the spec: filing-year dating, first-listed filter, base window t-5..t-1 (line 17), forward window t+1..t+3 (line 19), year t excluded, duplicate removal, per-firm grouping, the empty-base NA and no-forward 0 rules, and the deduplicated output with the five specified columns. The line 12 comment says missing classes contribute nothing, but the code does the opposite; the fix is to drop those rows (pc <- pc[!is.na(cpc_subclass)]).
